settings.name_in_paper: Clustered linear contextual bandits (n users in m unknown clusters)
unmapped: n users partitioned into m unknown clusters, each cluster sharing an unknown parameter u_j with ||u_j||=1
user i_t drawn uniformly at random from V each round
context vectors drawn i.i.d. on unit sphere from process with E[XX^T] of minimal eigenvalue lambda>0, number c_t chosen adaptively
noise conditionally zero mean with variance at most sigma^2, payoffs in [-1,1]
theoretical confidence bounds use lambda, n, and delta
settings.definition_quote: the learner receives a user index $i_t \in V$ together with a set of context vectors $C_{i_t} = \{\bx_{t,1}, \ldots,\bx_{t,c_t}\} \subseteq \R^d$. ... $a_i(\bx) = \bu_{j(i)}^\top\bx + \epsilon_{j(i)}(\bx)$ ... $r_t = \left(\max_{\bx \in C_{i_t} }\, \bu_{j(i_t)}^\top\bx\right) - \bu_{j(i_t)}^\top{\bar \bx_{t}}$

symbols.S_v: sum_{j=1}^m sqrt(v_j/(lambda n)), v_j cluster sizes

conditions: contexts i.i.d. with ||X||=1, E[XX^T] full rank with min eigenvalue lambda > 0
(z^T X)^2 conditionally sub-Gaussian with variance parameter <= lambda^2/(8 log(4c)), c_t <= c
noise conditionally zero mean with variance <= sigma^2; payoffs in [-1,1]
tuning: CB replaced by theoretical TCB and sTCB with delta replaced by delta/10.5

source.label: t:regret
source.quote: Then with probability at least $1-\delta$ the cumulative regret satisfies \sum_{t=1}^T r_t = {\tilde O}\Biggl( (\sigma\sqrt{d}+1)\,\sqrt{m}\,\Biggl(\frac{n}{\lambda^2}+\sqrt{T}\Bigl(1+\sum_{j=1}^m \sqrt{\frac{v_j}{\lambda\,n}} \Bigl)\Biggl) + \left(\frac{n}{\lambda^2} + \frac{n\,\sigma^2\,d\,}{\lambda\gamma^2} \right)\,\E[SD(\bu_{i_t})] + m \Biggl) ... In the above, the ${\tilde O}$-notation hides $\log (1/\delta)$, $\log m$, $\log n$, and $\log T$ factors.

results.notes: Õ hides log(1/delta), log m, log n, log T. sigma is a variance bound so mapped to sigma_std. Remark 4 says the result extends to sparse Erdos-Renyi initial graphs when clusters are large. Horizon marked anytime since the algorithm's confidence bounds do not use T (somewhat uncertain).
